issues.description: run() loop has no progress invariant — train() may not advance global_step, risking non-termination
issues.detail: The outer while loop in run() depends on train() advancing global_step. But train() iterates a finite data iterator of length save_interval; if the iterator yields zero batches (empty shard, exhausted state, off-by-one in build_iter), global_step is unchanged and the loop spins forever, re-saving the same checkpoint. No termination function is stated or enforced. UNREASONED.

issues.description: trainer_args key mismatch: docstring says max_steps, code reads max_step — precondition is unstated and unchecked
issues.detail: The constructor's docstring promises trainer_args contains max_steps, log_interval, val_interval, save_interval. The code reads trainer_args["max_step"] (singular) and never reads val_interval. The author cannot state a coherent precondition on trainer_args. A KeyError at construction is the optimistic outcome; a silently wrong config is the pessimistic one. UNREASONED.

issues.description: Checkpoint sort key parses 'step_' substring rather than the directory name, admitting malformed paths
issues.detail: split("step_")[-1] returns the tail after the last 'step_' in the basename. For a directory accidentally named 'step_3_backup' this yields '3_backup' and int() raises; for 'foo_step_10' it returns '10' and is silently accepted. The intended invariant — directory names are exactly 'step_<int>' — is neither stated nor checked. Use a regex with full-match and skip non-matches.

issues.description: valid() divides by len(value) without proving the list is non-empty; empty validation set crashes with ZeroDivisionError
issues.detail: If a validation factory yields zero batches (empty shard on a given rank, filtered split), all_stats is empty and the dict-comprehension is vacuous — safe. But if any iterator yields batches on some ranks and zero on others, all_reduce inside the loop deadlocks because participating ranks differ. The collective-call invariant (all ranks must call all_reduce the same number of times) is not established.

issues.description: _all_reduce_stats assumes every rank passes identical keys in identical order; this is asserted nowhere
issues.detail: The function iterates `for key in stats` and issues a collective per key. Correctness of NCCL all_reduce requires every rank to call the same collectives in the same order on tensors of the same shape and dtype. If stats keys differ across ranks (e.g., a rank skipped a metric on an empty batch), the program hangs or corrupts. State and enforce the precondition: stats keys are globally identical.

issues.description: main() uses torch.cuda.set_device(args.local_rank) when local_rank may be None
issues.detail: args.local_rank defaults to None. Under torchrun the LOCAL_RANK env var is set but the CLI flag is not, so unless the launcher injects --local_rank, set_device(None) is called before init_distributed and behavior is undefined. Precondition on the launch contract is unstated. Read LOCAL_RANK from env as the documented fallback and assert non-None.

review.summary: This is TESTED-NOT-PROVED at best, and largely UNREASONED. The author cannot state a coherent precondition on trainer_args — the docstring and the code disagree on the very key that bounds the training loop. The main termination function (global_step monotonically approaching max_step) is asserted by hope rather than by invariant; an empty training iterator turns run() into a silent infinite loop that helpfully overwrites the checkpoint each pass. The collective-communication discipline is not established: _all_reduce_stats and valid() both presume identical call sequences across ranks without ever stating or checking that precondition, which is precisely the failure mode that hangs distributed jobs at 3am. Checkpoint discovery parses substrings instead of validating names. REFUSED until the author can write, in one paragraph, the precondition on trainer_args, the loop invariant of run(), the termination function, and the collective-call discipline that _all_reduce_stats requires of its callers.
